--- title: "Recovery curves by age band (≤2, 2–5, 5–10, >10 years) × origin × registration status" description: "How does VAT (ICMS) recovery vary by the proposal's age bands, by origin and by registration status?" date: 2026-11-04 jupyter: python3 --- **Status:** exploration. Aggregates only. ::: {.callout-warning title="The register is later than the debts"} Registration status is the status on the register date printed by the setup cell. That date is after the debts and after the payments. A firm may be closed because of the debt. The status is not a cause measured before the outcome. ::: ::: {#setup .cell execution_count=1} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Source: VAT (ICMS) legal-entity extract, DuckDB read only. Window: 2016–2025. Rows after 2025 stay out of every table and every figure. Suppression: a cell with 1 to 4 distinct CNPJs is pooled as 'others (suppressed)'. A pool that still has fewer than 5 CNPJs is left blank. The count of pooled cells is printed with each table. Q1. Active = RFB code 02 (ATIVA). Inactive = codes 01, 03, 04, 08 (nula, suspensa, inapta, baixada). No establishment match, a root-only match, or any other code = unknown. Unknown is not forced into collectable or uncollectable. Q2. Payment history uses unit cnpj_root, scope vat_icms, denominator enrolled_value. The share is payments over enrolled value in the 5 calendar years that end in the reference year. The threshold is 10%. The unit's CDAs in the December snapshot enter the sum. The history is VAT (ICMS) only. Q3. Reference dates requested: 31 December of 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024. A year with no December snapshot is printed and left out of the tables. December 2024 is a partial snapshot because of a known gap in the DEBITO extract (EQ-05). Later recovery is the next calendar year, and the sum from the next year through 2025, each divided by the December stock. Q4. Precedence: suspended → guaranteed → instalment → unknown → active_history → inactive_history → active_recent → inactive_no_history → active_old. Suspended is uncollectable first. The guaranteed line is always emitted and is empty. no guarantee table in the data; collectable share is understated. Q5. Age bands (0, 2], (2, 5], (5, 10], >10. A value equal to a break stays in the lower band (left-closed is false). Ages from 0 to the first break are the first band. Both readings are shown: the annual paid/stock rate, and the cumulative recovery of cohorts enrolled in the window. The band above the last break is not observable on those cohorts. Q6. The outcome is any payment in the year, the same outcome as model 1 of the payment section. When the eligible frame is larger than 100,000 certificate-years, the fit uses a stratified sample of that size (year, origin, and the payment outcome), seed 2026. Standard errors are HC1. Clustered standard errors by CNPJ root are the column beside them. This is an association. It is not a forecast. Q7. One lab entry per block. Q8. The proposal material reports mean collection 1.38% against a collectable share 27.05%. The material states neither the year nor the tax cut. This page does not reproduce those two figures. It reports the analogous VAT (ICMS) legal-entity account. Registry attributes are the RFB extract 2026-03, which is later than the debts. CNAE enters as the division (two digits). ``` ::: ::: ## Question How does the recovery of VAT (ICMS) certificates vary across the age bands in the proposal, and does that pattern differ by origin and by registration status? ## Data The setup cell prints the window, the band edges and the source. The annual rate uses every certificate with positive stock in a year inside the window, including certificates enrolled before the window. Those older certificates are what makes the oldest band observable. That base is wider than the December snapshot used by the collectable rule and by the December sections: a certificate that had stock during the year and is absent in December stays in the annual rate and out of the December base. The cell under the annual table prints both counts and the difference. The cumulative reading uses only cohorts enrolled inside the window. Registration status and the division of economic activity come from the same RFB join as the firm section: the manifest hash is checked, and a missing firm or a root-only match keeps its own category. ## Method The annual rate in band $b$, origin $o$ and year $t$ is $$r_{b,o,t}=\frac{\sum_i \mathrm{paid}_{i,t}}{\sum_i \mathrm{stock}_{i,t}}$$ for certificates with positive stock. The stock-weighted mean over the window is the same ratio with the sums taken over years. It is not the unweighted mean of the yearly rates. Age uses the lab convention that a break belongs to the lower band. The band labels and the breaks are printed by the setup cell. This entry does not change the age bands used by the earlier age sections. The cumulative reading, for a cohort enrolled inside the window, is the sum of payments up to the last observed year inside the band, divided by the enrolled value. The oldest band is emitted empty for these cohorts: the window is too short for a certificate enrolled inside it to reach that age. ## How to read In the annual chart, the horizontal axis is the calendar year and the vertical axis is paid divided by stock. Each line is an origin and an age band. Compare lines within a year. A higher line is a higher rate in that year. The rate is not cumulative, and it is not a hazard from enrolment. In the cumulative chart, the horizontal axis is the enrolment year and the vertical axis is cumulative paid divided by enrolled value, at the last observed age inside the band. The empty oldest band means the horizon is not observed. It does not mean the rate is zero. The status chart uses the register date printed above. Read it as a description of who holds the stock, not as a prediction. ::: {#tbl-annual .cell tbl-cap='Annual paid divided by stock, by year, age band and origin.' execution_count=2} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Cells pooled by the suppression rule: 8 Years in the table run from 2016 to 2025. ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}

``` Stock-weighted recovery by registration status and age band, declared origin. Blank cells are suppressed. ::: ::: ## What not to conclude The annual rate is not the cumulative recovery of a cohort, and the cumulative reading is not observed for the oldest band. Registration status is not the status at enrolment. A difference between bands is not an effect of age, because older certificates are those that were not paid earlier. The join does not use a natural-person identifier.
